artifacts.summary: Confirms milestone-ref-land.sh has no lifecycle caller; enumerates the exact 8-item reference set (script, suite, a stale suite-classification.data row not in the dispatch's named list, a comment-only credit in test-milestone-review-handoff.sh, two manifest rows, two context docs); finds review-stack-prepare.sh already implements the identical ref-plumbing idiom and should become the re-pointed worked-implementation citation; and confirms tasks 691/692/693 (the handoff-printing territory) are already completed, so no ordering edge is needed.

memory_candidates.content: ref-plumbing-landing.md's Audience-line 'worked implementation' citation can go stale silently when the actual call site migrates: review-stack-prepare.sh (commit-tree + compare-and-swap update-ref at the review-ref build/restack sites) superseded milestone-ref-land.sh as the pattern's live use-site, discovered only by grepping for the idiom's two primitives across scripts/, not by any existing lint. When retiring a script that a pattern doc names as its 'worked implementation', grep for the same primitives elsewhere in the codebase before concluding the pattern itself is now unanchored.

scripts/tests/suite-classification.data (core extension) is NOT checked for stale rows by lint-unit-integration-boundary.sh in a way that fails the exit code -- a row naming a suite no longer discovered under tests/ logs as an [INFO] 'stale classification row' and does not affect the 0/1 exit verdict. So deleting a test file without also removing its classification row will not break CI/lint verification, but leaves dead data the file's own header discipline (every discovered suite gets a row, kept in sync) argues against leaving.
